title: One rule for a control that speaks for several picked things
goal: Every control in the panel now says the word Mixed the same way, but nothing says what a control should DO when the things you have picked disagree, or when there is more than one of them. So each new control settles it again on its own: a switch shows plain off, a component section vanishes rather than speaking for two copies, and a width field keeps showing a number the layers refused. Write the rule down once, so the three tasks waiting behind it stop each inventing an answer.
notes:
Design review 2026-09-05. Evidence: queue/audits/2026-09-04-mixed-one-look.json rough 2, 3, 4 and 5 all report a control answering the several-things question its own way after the one-look pass shipped; queue/audits/2026-09-04-copy-own-color.json rough 1 reports the whole Component section vanishing on a second copy. Unblocks the-knobs-panel-speaks-for-several-copies-at-onc (p2), a-switch-says-mixed-the-way-every-other-control (p3) and a-width-the-layers-refused-stops-claiming-the-nu (p3), each of which currently has to decide this for itself. The look is already settled and lives in MixedLook.style / MixedValue.text with the rule in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, next to the rungs written by one-rule-for-a-control-that-cannot-do-anything on 2026-09-04. This is the behaviour half of that same section.

Read the existing "What Mixed looks like" section first: it is good and it already says that a control saying Mixed is still a control and reaches every picked layer in one undo step. This task is the part it does not cover: what a control does when it cannot speak for the selection at all, what a field shows after a set that some of the picked layers refused, and the switch, which has no mixed position on the Mac. Write it as a sibling section, not a rewrite.
acceptance: The panel rules gain one short section covering a control over several picked things: what it reads when they agree, what it reads when they do not, what setting it does, and what a control does when it cannot speak for the picked things at all
It says what a control shows after a set that some of the picked things refused, since a field showing a number nothing has is the bug behind one of the tasks waiting on this
It says what a switch does, which is the one control with no mixed position on the Mac, so the next person does not have to decide that in the middle of a feature

It says when disappearing is the right answer and when speaking for the selection is, because the Component section disappearing on a second copy is the current behaviour and the rule has to either bless it or call it a bug
Every existing example named in the rule points at a real control in the app, and the three open tasks it unblocks are named in it
No app code changes in this task: it is the written rule, and the tasks behind it do the building

log.note: Adversarial review of the idea before writing. Risk 1: a rules doc nobody reads. Mitigated by siblinging it to the two sections it extends and by writing a pointer into all three unblocked task files, so the runner meets the rule before it meets the code. Risk 2: over-specifying a general theory of multi-select. Cut to the four things acceptance names, hung off one table. Risk 3: choosing the switch's look without the user. Every clause is DERIVED from rules the user already has (the segmented-row precedent for a control with no room for a word, MixedLook.style for the weight, the mixed-checkbox press cycle from the platform), not invented, and the p3 build task still ships a real capture the user can react to.

Checked the doc against the app before writing rather than after. Speaking-for-a-subset is already shipped practice (shadowReachNote, borderReachNote, ColorStyleSelection.members vs selectionCount/capableCount), so most of the rule DESCRIBES what is already right and only three gaps are new. One draft bullet was wrong and got corrected: I first wrote that a single control never leaves a section its siblings stay in, but colorRowSlots in EditorState+ColorStyles.swift already drops the Fill row when nothing picked has a fill while the Color section and Outline row stay, and that is correct. The rule now says the thing that leaves is the thing whose property is absent, and nothing larger.

Wrote docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, 'What a control DOES for several picked things', as a sibling after 'What Mixed looks like' and before 'A control that cannot act'. One table (reaches all/some/none) plus consequences, then two sub-sections: 'What a control shows after a set the picked things refused' and 'What a switch does, since a Mac switch has no third position'. Added one preview bullet at the top of section 4. Verdicts the three waiting tasks no longer have to reach: the Component section vanishing on a second copy is a BUG; copies of two different components keep the section and one sentence rather than going blank, since a knob is the same knob only when it is the same property of the same thing, never when it merely shares a name; a field reads back after the commit, never a landing computed before it; the switch stays a switch and says Mixed beside its caption, first press resolves to on.

Verified every symbol and every quoted string against the source: MixedValue.text, MixedLook.style, ColorStyleSelection.members/selectionCount/capableCount, colorRowSlots, shadowReachNote (quote is exact), borderReachNote, ShadowInspector/hasShadowEverywhere, the 'Enable Shadow' caption, LayersPanel component gate on selectedLayer, GeometryField.land() computing landing(parsed) before commit(parsed). No em dashes in the section. Scripts/test.sh green (exit 0), though no app code changed. No audit: acceptance forbids app changes, so there is nothing to playtest.

Wrote docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, 'What a control DOES for several picked things', as a sibling of 'What Mixed looks like'. One table (a control reaches all, some or none of the picked things) plus two sub-sections settling the two cases the look rule could not: a field reads back what the layers took after the commit rather than echoing what was typed, and a switch stays a switch and says Mixed beside its own caption with the first press resolving to on. Disappearing is blessed only as the 'none' answer, so the Component section vanishing on a second copy is named a bug, and copies of two different components keep the section with one sentence rather than going blank. All three unblocked tasks are named in the rule and each now carries a pointer back to it. Verified every symbol and quoted string against the source; Scripts/test.sh green; no app code, per acceptance.
